tool_uses.command:
cat >> /private/var/folders/pv/m1k13gmn189d64ndtxdbzrjc0000gn/T/wk/lsYnWg/printkit-vYfBsy/CHANGES.md <<'EOF'

## Round 1

Findings addressed: all 18 failing held-out cases listed in REVIEW.md (round 0). Items 1-6 of the review were already met and are unchanged in substance.

- Order: the result now follows the order typed (`"5,1-3"` is `[5, 1, 2, 3]`, `"3,1"` is `[3, 1]`, `"10,4-5,1"` is `[10, 4, 5, 1]`). It is no longer sorted.
- Repeats: pages are kept as many times as typed (`"2,2"` is `[2, 2]`, `"1-3,2"` is `[1, 2, 3, 2]`, `"1-2,1-2"` is `[1, 2, 1, 2]`). Nothing is de-duplicated.
- Backward ranges: `"5-3"` is `[5, 4, 3]`, `"2-1"` is `[2, 1]`, `"1,5-3"` is `[1, 5, 4, 3]`. No longer a RangeError.
- Open ends: `"8-"` runs to `pageCount` and `"-3"` starts at 1 (`"10-"` is `[10]`, `"-1"` is `[1]`, `"1,8-"` is `[1, 8, 9, 10]`). An open end still needs the given end to be a valid page, so `"11-"`, `"-11"` and `"-0"` are RangeErrors. A lone `"-"` stays a RangeError.
- Empty text: `""` and blank text (`"   "`) give every page, `1..pageCount`. Empty parts inside non-blank text (`"1,"`, `",1"`, `"1,,3"`, `","`) are still RangeErrors, since REVIEW.md settles only the whole-text case.
- Tests: replaced the tests that locked in the old choices (sorting, de-duplication, backward, open and empty rejections) with tests for the cases above; kept the TypeError and out-of-range tests.
- README.md: the `parseRanges` section now documents order, repeats, backward ranges, open ends, empty text, and what still throws.
EOF
